text:
anya: heads-up — edge quickstart types disappear after the bundling step. node dev is fine, edge bundle yields `any` for generics.

matt: can you paste the tiny repro?

anya: simplified: we have a retry helper typed as overloads:
function withRetry<T>(fn: ()=>Promise<T>): Promise<T>;
function withRetry(fn){ return retryWrapper(fn); }

call site: const u = await withRetry(()=> sdk.getUser<{id:string}>(id))

in local node build `u` is `{id:string}`. after the edge bundle `u` is `any`.

ravi: sounds like the bundler is flattening d.ts and the SDK's conditional exports + cjs fallback are confusing tsc inference. especially with `export =` or mixed `types` targets.

zoe: overloads + generics are fragile when declaration shapes change. if the types file loses a single clear signature, inference will widen.

matt: short-term sample fixes: 1) pin tsconfig moduleResolution to `node` for the sample build; 2) ensure package exports `types` points explicitly to the ESM typings used by edge; 3) avoid overloads in helpers — use a single generic signature: `function withRetry<T>(fn: ()=>Promise<T>, opts?:RetryOpts): Promise<T>`.

anya: added a minimal repro in the repo and a draft PR that updates the sample tsconfig and the edge CI workflow to run rollup + `tsc`. also added a README note under "Edge bundlers & TS".

pkg-bot: CI: node-cjs typecheck OK. edge-bundle typecheck failed on master at 2601122300; branch `devex/edge-ts-repro` shows passing with sample tsconfig change.

ravi: long-term: SDK should avoid dual export shapes that lead to ambiguous declaration merging, or ship a small `types/edge.d.ts` entry to make the edge path explicit.

zoe: add a lint rule for samples forbidding `as any` / `// @ts-ignore` to prevent users from hiding the issue in onboarding code.

anya: will link the PR and the repro issue here. TL;DR: generics + overloads + conditional exports + bundler rewriting = ambiguous inference in edge builds; plan is sample config fixes + CI + SDK cleanup.
